title: Lazarus brought forward as proof of the wonder-worker
english: Rightly did the nursling of the truth bring back into the open the man who a little before had been bound in the prison of Hades, who had leapt out and mocked the bonds of death by the defeat of death, who had been set free from his grim burial wrappings. Passing over all the others who were eating with him, he listed him by name. For the evangelist's aim was not to beautify Christ, the one proclaimed through him, through Christ's keeping company and sharing meals with distinguished persons, nor to report things that would win favor, but to make the wonder-working God known to all through his own works. And this work was Christ's, and the greatest of his works was the raising of Lazarus, who had been dissolved and poured out into corruption.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG 18 Homilia christologica in Lazarum u01-rem-early
orientation: The preacher is expounding John's account of the supper at Bethany, where Lazarus, recently raised from the dead, reclined at table with Jesus.

title: Lazarus at table as living proof
english: That is why John shows him dining with the Lord. He proclaims to the whole world that the wonder was not a phantom. He makes the marvel a feast, the feast of that splendid banquet where Lazarus lay before the guests as an early gift, spiritual food for those at table. At that marvelous supper the pleasure of the belly was held back, and the souls of those reclining there feasted. In that marvelous joy the man who had been made a table for corruption became once more, for living men, a table full of marvels.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG 18 Homilia christologica in Lazarum u01-rem-mid
orientation: John the Evangelist is presenting Lazarus dining with Jesus as proof that his resurrection was real.

title: Lazarus shown whole and the saving will
english: It was only right for him to act in this way. He holds riches for every need, and good gifts pour from his will like water from a spring that never runs dry. He had entered under a poor roof, so it was fitting for him to add wealth to their poverty. He had done the same at Cana in Galilee, when he gave wine that no field had grown. In the same way it was fitting for him to lead that freed man into their midst at just the right hour, and to lay him open before the children like a paradise of rich feasting, where he both gave joy and shared it.

In Lazarus no stench of decay remained. A divine call had given him a share in imperishable fragrance. No wound or ruin showed in his limbs. His Maker had formed him anew in a moment. No mark, small or great, was left of the kind that change stamps on bodies lowered to the grave. His frame stood whole on every side, complete and beautiful to the very hair.

So he fittingly fed that gladness. I mean it sprang both from the pure love of those blameless hosts and from the miracles of a God fully revealed. For Martha knew, she knew well, what delights the gaze of God above all else: if the Savior who has received kindness … [the text breaks off here]. She had heard this from his own lips. For Jesus says, "My food is to do the will of him who sent me" (John 4:34). And the will of the Father and the Son is the salvation of men. That salvation is faith in him who is glorified forever on high with the Father and the Holy Spirit. As Jesus says in the Gospels, "This is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks on the Son and believes in him should have eternal life" (John 6:40).

orientation: The preacher is still using Lazarus at table as proof that his resurrection was real, just before turning to the saying about fire.
